{{short description|French mathematician (1843–1913)}}
[[File:GTarry.jpeg|thumb|Gaston Tarry]]
'''Gaston Tarry''' (27 September 1843 – 21 June 1913) was a French [[mathematician]]. Born in [[Villefranche de Rouergue]], [[Aveyron]], he studied [[mathematics]] at high school before joining the [[civil service]] in [[Algeria]]. He pursued mathematics as an [[amateur]].

== Contributions ==
In 1895 Tarry published a systematic algorithm for traversing a maze without prior knowledge of its layout; this method is now recognized in [[graph theory]] as one of the earliest variants of a [[depth-first search]] (DFS) algorithm.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Tarry |first=Gaston |year=1895 |title=Le problème des labyrinthes |journal=Nouvelles Annales de Mathématiques |series=Série 3 |volume=14 |pages=187&ndash;190}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Even |first=Shimon |year=2011 |title=Graph Algorithms |edition=2nd |publisher=Cambridge University Press |pages=46&ndash;48 |isbn=978-0-521-73653-4}}</ref>

Tarry also made contributions to [[Number theory|number theory]] and [[Combinatorics|combinatorics]], including work on the [[Prouhet–Tarry–Escott problem]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Tarry |first=Gaston |year=1898 |title=Question 1401 |journal=L'Intermédiaire des Mathématiciens |volume=5 |pages=266&ndash;267}}</ref>

In 1900 Tarry confirmed [[Leonhard Euler]]'s conjecture that no 6×6 [[Graeco-Latin square#Thirty-six officers problem|Graeco-Latin square]] was possible (the [[Mutually_orthogonal_Latin_squares#Thirty-six_officers_problem|36 officers problem]]).<ref>{{cite web |title=From Latin Squares to Sudoku: A History of Magic Numbers |url=http://www1.hollins.edu/faculty/clarkjm/M471/From%20Latin%20Squares%20to%20Sudoku.ppt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081001193239/http://www1.hollins.edu/faculty/clarkjm/M471/From%20Latin%20Squares%20to%20Sudoku.ppt |archive-date=2008-10-01 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=36 Officer Problem |url=http://academic.scranton.edu/faculty/doughertys1/euler.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080828085817/http://academic.scranton.edu/faculty/doughertys1/euler.htm |archive-date=2008-08-28 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | first = Gaston | last = Tarry | title = Le problème des 36 officiers | journal = Comptes rendus de l'Association française pour l'avancement des sciences | volume = 29 | number = 1 | pages = 122&ndash;123 | year = 1900 | url = https://hdl.handle.net/2027/njp.32101076521697?urlappend=%3Bseq=242%3Bownerid=27021597768906376-252}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | first = Gaston | last = Tarry | title = Le problème des 36 officiers | journal = Comptes rendus de l'Association française pour l'avancement des sciences | volume = 29 | number = 2 | pages = 170&ndash;203 | year = 1901 | url = https://hdl.handle.net/2027/hvd.32044106224272?urlappend=%3Bseq=182%3Bownerid=27021597765797130-188}}</ref>
